ANNEX.text:
[STICKY NOTE]

If my door is locked and my laptop is here: I have gone to the pens.

If my door is locked and my laptop is gone: so am I.

— ${c.lost}
ANNEX.title: Gone to the Pens

ANNEX.text:
[LOUD STATIC]

...${c.lead} here.

The corridor walls are absorbing sound.
I yelled for ${c.custodian} earlier and the echo... didn't come back.
It just stopped.

[CLICK]
ANNEX.title: Unresponsive Echo
Doors
UNSENT MAIL #1
Observation Report #1

ARCHIVE.title: Hide and Seek

ARCHIVE.text:
[SHELVING MEMO]

Whoever is doing it, please stop filing the ${P} reports under FICTION.

P.S. I know it's you, ${c.custodian}. The whispering in the stacks is NOT related to the documents, and even if it were, they would not appreciate the joke.

Be warned: I'm not responsible for what might happen to you if you keep messing around with the records.

That's not a threat; it's a professional courtesy. Knock it off.

- ${c.archivist}
ARCHIVE.title: Fact, not Fiction!
Floor Plan Request

INCINERATOR.text:
[COMBUSTION LOG #509-${hours}]

- Burned four (4) carts of `${P}` related paperwork at Hour #${hrs} of Week #${WEEK}.
- Charged weight in: 10.8 kilos.
- Charged weight out: 11 kilos.

NOTES: I weighed everything twice to confirm the impossible, this time.

We are burning less paper than we are producing ash.

- ${c.custodian}
INCINERATOR.title: Combustion Log #1

INCINERATOR.text:
[ROAR OF COMBUSTION, THEN IT DROPS OUT ENTIRELY]

...hour ${hrs}.

${c.archivist} was right.
Kill the burners and the sound underneath them doesn't stop.
It isn't a machine.

It's a lung.

[STATIC]
INCINERATOR.title: Lung Burner

INCINERATOR.text:
FLUE INSPECTION #${ctx.seed}

STATUS: DEFERRED

NOTES: The stack runs eleven levels on the drawing and only nine in the facility.

Contractor says the drawing is wrong because Contractor has already been paid.

I have measured the outside and inside of this structure twice now and I would like someone to tell me which two floors I am actually standing between, and which two floors are missing.
INCINERATOR.title: Flue Inspection

BOARDROOM.text:
[PERFORMANCE NOTE]

SUBJECT: ${c.lost}

DESCRIPTION: Subject's last review was flagged as an "excessive interest in the building itself."

Subject was then reassigned to the pens. Suspiciously, the subject had requested the reassignment in writing, in advance, before it was even proposed by HQ.

Signed,
CHIEF DEPUTY OFFICER
~~REDACTED~~
BOARDROOM.title: Excessive Interest

BOARDROOM.text:
[TWELVE CHAIRS BEING PULLED OUT, COUNTED ALOUD]

...eleven.

[PAUSE]

Eleven of us just stood up.
Everybody sit down and please explain to me why I just heard twelve of you stand.

[CLICK]
BOARDROOM.title: Musical Chairs
Quarterly Review

BOARDROOM.text:
[SEATING CHART, AMENDED IN PENCIL]

The chart shows twelve chairs, but there are only eleven names on the roster. The twelfth was never assigned a member, but it has never been empty at the start of a meeting.

${c.lead} asked us to stop counting, because nobody can figure out who isn't supposed to be there.
BOARDROOM.title: Seating Chart

SERVER.text:
OUTBOUND TRAFFIC SUMMARY [UNSIGNED]

Sustained upstream at hour ${hrs} with no session open and no user logged.

Payload is not encrypted, but nothing decipherable, either.

The carrier tone sits at the same frequency as the fan wash and I only found it because I turned the fans OFF and it was still there.
SERVER.title: Traffic Note

SERVER.text:
[HANDWRITTEN NOTE]

Do not reboot Rack 09. I know what the ticket says; ignore it!

It has been turned off since we opened and it is STILL hot. 

— ${c.custodian}
SERVER.title: Rack 09

SERVER.text:
[FAN WASH, THEN SUDDEN SILENCE AS IT IS CUT]

...there.

Fans are off. You can hear it now.

That's not cooling.

That's a carrier and it's been under the fan noise this whole time.

[STATIC]
SERVER.title: Cooling Fan

SERVER.text:
THERMAL EXCEPTION REPORT: RACK 14

The cold aisle is holding, and the hot aisle is holding, but the bugger room between them is four degrees warmer than either, which is not a thing thermodynamics are allowed to do.

Filed with facilities. Facilities filed it back with no notes.

-${c.custodian}
SERVER.title: Cold Aisle

CHECKPOINT.text:
CHECKPOINT GATE LOG, LANE #3

${hrs}: ${c.lost} scanned IN.
No corresponding OUT.

Lane #3 has processed forty-one OUT scans since, against forty IN.

${c.archivist} says the discrepancy is likely just a rounding error.

A human disappearing is not something that can be explained away as a "rounding error." ...Can it?
CHECKPOINT.title: Gate Log 1

CHECKPOINT.text:
[LAMINATED NOTE]

Count your gear on the way back. If you return with a suit you did not leave with, hang it up and say nothing.

If you return with two, come find me.

— ${c.custodian}
CHECKPOINT.title: Gear Note

CHECKPOINT.text:
[GATE CYCLING REPEATEDLY, NOBODY PASSING]

...forty-one out, forty in, and the gate is still counting. 

${c.lost} scanned in at hour ${hrs} and the machine still thinks they're inside.

So do I.

[CLICK]
CHECKPOINT.title: 41 In, 40 Out

ATRIUM.text:
LOST PROPERTY SLIP: BALCONY, TIER 9

FOUND: One (1) staff badge, ${c.lost}, face down on a table set for two.

NOTE: Tier 9 has no stairs, no lift and no floor plan entry. 

This slip was filed by ${c.custodian}, who declines to say how they got up there.
ATRIUM.title: Lost Property

ATRIUM.text:
[PA ANNOUNCEMENT, TRANSCRIBED]

"The atrium will close in fifteen minutes."

NOTE: Plays at five minute intervals, but has never once counted down from fifteen.

${c.archivist} timed it against the hum and they are the same wavelength frequency.
ATRIUM.title: PA Announcement

ATRIUM.text:
[A CART WHEEL TICKING, FAR BELOW]

...I walked up.

That's the part I need on record.

There is no stair to this tier and I walked up, and I can see the aisles from here, and they are not where the planogram says.


[CLICK]
ATRIUM.title: Planogram Tiers

ATRIUM.text:
SHELF PLANOGRAM: REVISION #6

Aisles run north to south on the current plan. I have tried to have them run east to west since the second revision, but I have stopped issuing revisions because, no matter what, the aisles are not being moved. 

The plan is being corrected, after the fact, by somebody who gets here before I do.

I give up!

- ${c.archivist}
ATRIUM.title: Revision #6

CLINIC.text:
[INTAKE FORM, INCOMPLETE]

PATIENT: ${c.lost}
PRESENTING: "Spatial disagreement."

NOTES: Patient could describe the route here accurately but could not walk it twice. Patient was calm about this.

I was not.
CLINIC.title: Spatial Disagreement

CLINIC.text:
[AUDIOLOGY REFERRAL]

STATUS: DECLINED

REASON: Six staff reporting a persistent low tone. All six pass the hearing screen. The tone is not in their ears.

I have written that sentence four times now and it does not get easier to file, because I hear it too but cannot tell where it is coming from.
CLINIC.title: Unknowable Hum

CLINIC.text:
[WARD ROUNDS: HOUR ${hrs}]

Bed four's chart updates overnight in handwriting that matches ${c.lost}'s.

Just thought somebody should know.

- ${c.lead}
CLINIC.title: Ward Rounds

MAINTENANCE.text:
[DUCT INSPECTION, SECTION 12]

The return line carries a tone at the far end that does not come from any plant on the drawing

Cut the fans, tone stays.

Cut the power, tone stays.

Cut the shit, *I* say!
MAINTENANCE.title: Cut the Shit

MAINTENANCE.text:
[STATIC]

[Unintelligible whispering]

[Blood Curdling Scream]

[Random Synth Tone Melody]

[CLICK]
MAINTENANCE.title: Random Tones

MAINTENANCE.text:
[SHAFT SURVEY]

I ran the tape down and it read one hundred and six meters. Ran it again back up the other way and it suddenly read ninety-eight.

Same tape, same shaft, same afternoon.

Unfortunately, I can't file a work order against with faulty arithmetic.
MAINTENANCE.title: Shaft Survey

CHASM.text:
[RAIL NOTICE, WIRED TO THE HANDRAIL]

Do not lean out and look for the bottom.

There is one. That is not the problem. 

The problem is how long you will stand there once you have found it.

— ${c.custodian}
CHASM.title: Rail Notice
Chasm Sighting

CHASM.text:
[CATWALK LOAD CERTIFICATION, VOIDED]

NOTICE: Span was certified at twenty-two metres. Actual span measures thirty-one under load and twenty-two unloaded, which is backwards, and I would like that noted and addressed before anybody walks on it again.
CHASM.title: Catwalk Verification

DEFAULT.text:
[INCIDENT LOG]

Subject exhibited extreme paranoia after ${hrs} hours. Claimed the hum of the fluorescent lights was a linguistic sequence.

We cut the power, but the humming didn't stop.

Neither did the subject's delusions.
DEFAULT.title: Hum Incident

DEFAULT.text:
[MEMO]

If you hear it scraping, stand still.

If you hear it breathing, turn off the light.

If you hear it laughing, close your eyes.
DEFAULT.title: Warning

DEFAULT.text:
${c.lead} says the exits are a motivational tool.
${c.archivist} says the exits are load-bearing.

${c.lost} said the exits are a rumor the building spreads about itself.
${c.lost} was smiling when they said it. 

Nobody has seen that smile since.
DEFAULT.title: Paranoid Memo

DEFAULT.text:
MAINTENANCE REQUEST
FILED BY: ${c.custodian}

Please send someone to Level 0. The carpet is damp again.

Also, stop leaving geometry in the negative coordinate space.
DEFAULT.title: Negative Space Complaint

DEFAULT.text:
[CAFETERIA NOTICE]

The almond water is not a beverage.

The almond water is a countermeasure.

Ration accordingly.

— ${c.custodian}
DEFAULT.title: Cafeteria Notes

IMPOUND.text:
[CHAINLINK SHIVERING]

...I found ${c.lost}'s recorder in the cage.
It's still spinning.
There's no tape inside it.
I'm recording this onto the outside of that, somehow.

[CLICK]
IMPOUND.title: Lost Recorder
Meepis

EXIT.title: Custodial Shifts

EXIT.text:
COFFEE FUND HONESTY BOX

Balance carried forward: $340.03
Contributions this month: $0.00
Withdrawals this month: $0.00

[Taped Underneath]: "Nobody has taken any and nobody has added any since ${c.lost} stopped showing up. I refuse to close the account."
EXIT.title: Coffee Fund

EXIT.text:
**LAMINATED INSTRUCTIONS, WALL-MOUNTED BESIDE THE CAR**

DEBRIEF SCRIPT — READ ALOUD, DO NOT PARAPHRASE!

1. "You are at the extraction point."
2. "You are going up."
3. "Do not describe what you saw until you are asked."
4. [This entry has been violently scratched out.]
EXIT.title: Debrief Script

EXIT.text:
BIRTHDAY CARD, UNSEALED

Front: a cartoon of a filing cabinet wearing a party hat.

Inside, eleven signatures in eleven different pens, and under them in ${c.archivist}'s hand: "Many happy returns, and I mean RETURNS, ${c.custodian}.

Sign yourself out this time."
EXIT.title: Birthday Card

EXIT.text:
MAINTENANCE COMPLAINT: CAR MUSIC

The hold music in the elevator car is nine seconds long and loops with a click. Over a full ascent you will hear it four hundred times. I have submitted this complaint eleven times.

It is nine seconds. Four hundred times nine is infinity. Or at least it might as well be.

Please.

- ${c.custodian}
EXIT.title: Maintenance Complaint

EXIT.text:
LOST AND FOUND — EXTRACTION DESK

1 × reading glasses, lens cracked
1 × wedding ring, cold
3 × single gloves, all left hand
1 × cassette, unlabelled, snapped
2 × mug, identical, both chipped in the same place

Unclaimed items are held ninety days and then held indefinitely, because nobody has ever come to the desk.
EXIT.title: Lost and Found

EXIT.text:
TAPED INSIDE THE SUPPLY LOCKER, HAND-DRAWN

A six-panel diagram showing how to fold a hazmat suit so it fits the shelf. Panel five is just an arrow and the word "PATIENCE."

Panel six is the folded suit, drawn with visible pride, and initialed.
EXIT.title: Hazmat Diagram
Extraction Note

ACME.text:
${P} FACILITIES MEMO
FROM: ${c.engineer}

Requisitioned six replacement fixtures for the ACME shaft after crews kept reporting the lower decks going dark. All six approved. All six installed.

The lower decks are still dark.

Whatever's lighting the top of that shaft holds steady no matter how far down you climb, directly overhead the whole way, like it's following you. It just stops reaching you somewhere around the fourth or fifth deck, same as it always has, fixtures or no fixtures.

I don't think this is a fixture problem. I don't know who to write that up to instead.

- ${c.engineer}
ACME.title: Solar Survey

ACME.text:
[BOOTS ON METAL GRATING, RECEDING]

...${c.lost} swears the drop has a bottom. Says you can see it from the fourth deck if the light's right.

I watched them climb down out of the light at hour ${hrs}.

I have not watched them climb back up.

[CLICK]
ACME.title: Last Rung

ACME.text:
[SITE FREQUENCY LOG]

Something below the lowest mapped deck is running. Not the sun; the sun makes no sound at all.

This is a low mechanical thrum, felt through the ladder rails more than heard.

${c.archivist} clocked it against the atrium PA loop out of curiosity. Same wavelength.

Neither of us knows what that's supposed to mean, and neither of us had said so out loud until now.
ACME.title: Site Frequency Log
Deck Count
